parts.text: Read puzzle.txt with read_file, solve its scheduling problem, and give a concise schedule and proof. Do not modify any files.

startup_tools.name: read_file
startup_tools.description: Read text with one-based inclusive start_line/end_line. Optional max_bytes bounds the read; job reports cap inline output and preserve the full result on disk.

startup_tools.name: list_directory
startup_tools.description: List immediate entries, sorted by name; directories end with /.

startup_tools.name: search_files
startup_tools.description: Search files recursively using a regular expression. context_lines defaults to zero. Output uses grep path:line:text and path-line-context with merged windows.

startup_tools.name: write_file
startup_tools.description: Write text, creating parent directories. Existing files require overwrite:true unless append:true. Append preserves existing content.

startup_tools.name: edit_file
startup_tools.description: Replace one exact, unique old_text anchor with new_text. Zero or multiple matches refuse without changing the file; read and provide a more specific anchor.

startup_tools.name: run_command
startup_tools.description: Start a fresh /bin/sh in a PTY. cwd applies only to this call, relative to the workspace. Merged output and exit_code stay on disk; a running report is a handle, not cancellation. ai_callback_delay is seconds (default 3); pattern matches unseen output; max_output_bytes defaults to 16384.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

startup_tools.name: wait_for_job
startup_tools.description: Wait for a job, including a finished job. Return only unseen output; waiting does not stop execution.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

startup_tools.name: send_input
startup_tools.description: Send a line of input to a running PTY job, then wait. A missing trailing newline is added.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

startup_tools.name: kill_job
startup_tools.description: Kill a job's process group. Go-only work is marked killed but its goroutine cannot be stopped.

startup_tools.name: tool_limits
startup_tools.description: Set one-shot wait/output limits for the very next call, whichever tool it is. That call reports consumption; explicit call arguments override these limits.

ai_callback_delay.description: Seconds before looking again, default 3; never a job deadline

startup_tools.name: micro_handoff
startup_tools.description: Checkpoint at a completed micro-goal. Write text with what succeeded, what failed, source locations and next steps. Removes all tool traffic but preserves conversation and this note.

startup_tools.name: keep_tool_results
startup_tools.description: Keep the previous batch of tool results instead of automatic stubbing on supported models. Does not keep results of tools called alongside this call.

parts.text:
Two identical workers, nonpreemptive jobs. Durations and prerequisites:
A: 4, none
B: 3, none
C: 5, A
D: 2, A
E: 4, B
F: 3, C and D
G: 2, D and E
H: 1, F and G
Find a minimum-makespan valid schedule. Justify optimality, not merely validity.
Keep both workers explicit in the answer, and verify every dependency before claiming optimality.

summary.text:
**Solving scheduling problem**

I need to solve this scheduling challenge with a total of 24 units, needing to adjust to 12. The sequence involves workers using different tasks, with worker 1 handling segments A, C, F, and H for a total time of 13. Worker 2 will work on B, E, D, and G, also totaling 13. I’ll prepare a clear table showcasing each worker's time slots while ensuring all prerequisites are satisfied. It seems pretty straightforward!

parts.text:
**Minimum makespan: 13 time units.**

| Worker | Schedule |
|---|---|
| 1 | A [0,4), C [4,9), F [9,12), H [12,13) |
| 2 | B [0,3), E [3,7), D [7,9), G [9,11) |

All prerequisites are satisfied: F starts after C and D finish; G starts after D and E finish; H starts after F and G finish.

**Optimality:** The prerequisite chain A → C → F → H requires \(4+5+3+1=13\) time units, so every valid schedule takes at least 13. This schedule achieves that bound.

| Worker | Schedule |
|---|---|
| 1 | A: 0–4; C: 4–9; F: 9–12; H: 12–13 |
| 2 | B: 0–3; E: 3–7; D: 7–9; G: 9–11; idle: 11–13 |

**Dependency verification** (finish ≤ successor’s start):
- A → C: \(4 \le 4\)
- A → D: \(4 \le 7\)
- B → E: \(3 \le 3\)
- C → F: \(9 \le 9\)
- D → F: \(9 \le 9\)
- D → G: \(9 \le 9\)
- E → G: \(7 \le 9\)
- F → H: \(12 \le 12\)
- G → H: \(11 \le 12\)

Each job runs uninterrupted for its required duration, with no overlap on either worker.

**Optimality:** The chain A → C → F → H takes \(4+5+3+1=13\) time units, so every valid schedule has makespan at least 13. This schedule finishes at 13, hence is optimal.
